answer: A protocol pairs each identity with a random counterpart for commit-reveal. Both submit sealed commitments before the gale of reveal opens; late reveals void the pair. Settlement splits rewards by diversity coefficient: pairs sharing a cluster fingerprint get discounted shares, cross-cluster pairs earn full rewards. Each vertex in the graph carries a cluster tag, so a farmer flooding clones into a haven of self-referential nodes finds most pairs intra-cluster, paying full compute for fractional returns. Clones cannot preselect counterparts since pairing is seed-derived after commitments close.
